purpose: Select the visually stronger candidate without allowing candidate history, model class, automated contour counts, or expected answer to bias the first human comparison.
scope: Comparative selection only. The supplied primary reference remains the sole likeness authority and the direct primary-contour gate remains independently required for acceptance.

contains: two anonymized candidate view sets labelled amber and cobalt
a blind reviewer prompt and response template
must_not_contain: candidate IDs, labels, paths, histories, provenance, model class, scores, overlays, trace metrics, source manifests or expected result
image metadata that identifies a source artifact
public_package.label_assignment: The operator tool deterministically assigns amber and cobalt from each candidate's view-byte fingerprint and review ID. The private mapping is outside public/ and is never shown to a phase-A reviewer.

review.required_context: A fresh reviewer context receives only the public package and is instructed not to inspect its parent, repository, history, metadata, overlay or operator mapping.

phase_a.decision: Choose amber, cobalt or indistinguishable by literal primary-view likeness. Record confidence and three visible reasons. No scalar score is allowed.

phase_b.decision: Confirm, reverse or mark indistinguishable after judging coherent volume, hidden defects and anatomy. Record only visible evidence.

phase_c.evidence: Direct locked-camera contour overlay and its exact metadata are disclosed only after phases A and B are recorded.
phase_c.decision: The technical contour gate may block acceptance for a material mismatch. It never converts a blind ordinal verdict into a numeric likeness score or reverses that verdict.

review.consensus: A comparative winner exists only when at least two phase-B reviewers select the same label. Any disagreement or indistinguishable result is inconclusive and requires another focused iteration or additional reviewers.
review.acceptance: A blind comparison never accepts a model on its own. Acceptance additionally requires the primary trace gate, normal-view defect review, relevant animation/material evidence and the project's explicit runtime/export gates.

metric_policy: Automated pixel counts are diagnostic evidence for the exact primary trace only. They are not a cross-class likeness score and cannot rank generated, trace-led or primitive candidates.
